SMTO-AUT-0031 — SMTO couldn't renew its access to your Google account

GUID: c9ad1ea5-8d07-5079-a083-c520f2dafecf
Slug: google-token-refresh-failed
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • SMTO needed to renew its saved access to your Google account and couldn't. This older message doesn't say why; it could be a network problem or a sign-in that needs renewing.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running SMTO is online and can reach Google, for example by opening a Google page in a browser on that computer. A temporary network problem can stop renewal even when nothing is wrong with your account.
  2. If your request was going to send, change or delete something, check in Google whether it already happened before asking again. This older message doesn't record what was done, so checking first avoids doing it twice.
  3. If renewal still fails, ask SMTO to reconnect the same Google account and sign in with the same email address. If Google stopped accepting SMTO's saved access, only a fresh sign-in for that account restores it.

What success looks like

  • Your Google request runs without asking you to sign in, or the reconnect page says your email is connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't connect a different Google account in place of this one.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Legacy compatibility alias google.token_refresh_failed: refreshing a saved Google token failed for an unrecorded reason; current refresh reports provider_unavailable, reauthorization_required or account_changed instead.

What this means

  • The historical token-refresh-failed alias remains recognized, while current refresh distinguishes provider exchange failure, rejected authorization and stale account updates. No direct current producer was found for this compatibility identity. It preserves historical meaning without inventing missing cause, scope or execution facts.

Why this can happen

  • The historical token-refresh-failed alias remains recognized, while current refresh distinguishes provider exchange failure, rejected authorization and stale account updates.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare retained provider availability, refresh rejection and account revision evidence; use the current specific failure when available.

How to fix it

  • This identity has no current producer, so look for the specific current error in the Server log. Check that the Server can reach https://oauth2.googleapis.com (provider_unavailable), and if Google rejects the refresh grant (reauthorization_required), reconnect the same account_key with auth.google_connect.
  • Check provider availability and reconnect the same account if refresh continues to fail.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account either refreshes successfully or completes deliberate reconnection after a confirmed grant problem.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.
